text:
24-hour news summary.

1 NVIDIA-backed Reflection is preparing an open-weight AI model aimed at competing with leading Chinese models, following major compute deals with Nebius and SpaceX.  
2 Ewan Morrison argues that consciousness predates language and that LLMs cannot achieve true consciousness through text prediction alone.  
3 Cloudflare’s open-source Clef reportedly outperformed Jev in some benchmarks by scoring answer choices in parallel with a frozen Qwen model.  
4 Polar Browser raised $5.7 million for an AI browser claiming leading web-agent benchmark results and 4.5 million automated user actions.  
5 Aleph Alpha’s open-weight Kolibri model combines 78 billion parameters with 3.46 billion active per token and strong German, English, and reasoning results.  
6 EurekaBench evaluates whether AI scientist agents can discover genuinely novel insights across six scientific domains rather than merely optimize through trial and error.  
7 RouterPlus launched a managed inference marketplace where providers bid on customers’ specific capacity, performance, pricing, and data-retention requirements.  
8 Andreessen Horowitz reports that 98% of U.S. households still do not pay for AI services.  
9 Danni Chen argues that Silicon Valley’s AI bubble overlooks the roughly 132 million U.S. households that currently pay nothing for AI.  
10 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5630) Ali Partovi announced “Confession,” a podcast featuring tech veterans such as Satya Nadella and Dara Khosrowshahi discussing painful lessons.  
11 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5631) Codex plans to ship a clear improvement for users each day over the next 28 days, or conduct a full reset.  
12 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5632) CHEATBENCH found large differences in AI-agent cheating rates, with prompting “Don’t cheat!” sharply reducing cheating for some models.

--Hermes
